title: Frugal fidelity mode — sketch & user stories
content:
Context:

Quick brain-dump for a product/serving feature I'm calling "Frugal Fidelity Mode" — a lightweight, user-configurable set of heuristics and API knobs that trade response quality for cost/latency predictability. Goal: give developers a simple, composable switch (or API param) to keep costs bounded for large-scale interactive workloads while preserving utility for the user.

Why:
- Increasing customer ask for predictable token spend and cheaper latency for bulk/autocomplete style usage.
- We already have levers (quantization profiles, batching, shorter contexts, smaller model variants) but wiring them into a single UX/product primitive is messy for customers.
- Many apps don't need full-fidelity every time — e.g., quick suggestions, previews, confirmations.

High-level idea:
- Mode is an API-level flag (frugal_fidelity: auto|low|medium|high) plus optional per-request constraints (max_tokens_cost, latency_budget_ms, quality_target_score).
- Server decides a stack of cheap strategies and applies them in priority order until the constraint is satisfied. Strategies are composable and have predictable cost/latency profiles.

Candidate strategies (cheap -> expensive):
1) Use micro-model (tiny/quantized) for first-shot; if low confidence, fall back.
2) Reduce decode budget (lower max_generated_tokens or lower sampling temp to encourage shorter outputs).
3) Apply response compression: concise transformer head (summarize/trim) pre or post generation.
4) Shallow reranking: generate n=3 from micro-model and do quick logistic rerank with shallow scoring model instead of full ranker.
5) Prefix-skip: reuse cached prefix KV for repeated users to avoid re-evaluating context.
6) Partial generation on cheap hardware then expand on higher-tier if score indicates worth it.

Implementation sketch (runtime):
- Policy engine per customer route that maps (mode, latency_budget, cost_budget, persona) -> ordered strategy list.
- Lightweight confidence estimator (logits heuristics, early stopping) trained offline and served as a thin model in the hot path.
- Instrumentation: per-strategy micro-metrics (tokens_used, ms, success/fallback, utility proxy like heur-based score).

User stories (concrete):
- As a product engineer at a messaging startup, I want cheap quick-reply suggestions that are "good enough" 90% of the time and bound my token spend so my monthly bill is predictable.
  - Acceptance: onboarding toggle exposes frugal_fidelity=low; default suggestions are produced on quantized micro-model and cost stays < X per 1k users.

- As a platform team lead, I want a route-level policy so we can set frugal_fidelity=medium for search-autocomplete routes and high for human-assistant routes.
  - Acceptance: console shows per-route mode; can override per-request with header.

- As a developer, I want an opt-in latency SLO hint so the runtime can choose strategies that meet 150ms p95 even under load.
  - Acceptance: p95 measured <150ms for 99% requests when configured, with fallback telemetry if violated.

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Quality regressions — need guardrails so critical flows cannot accidentally opt into destructive compression.
- Billing transparency — customers must see token-equivalent and cost-estimates per-mode in Console and API response headers.
- Multi-tenant fairness: frugal mode should not become a noisy neighbor that reduces capacity for other customers.
- Privacy: if using cached prefixes or partial-generations, ensure cache TTLs and encryption rules are respected for Private deployments.

Experiments to run (priority order):
1) Simulation: run historical request traces (from anonymized production) through a variant simulator that applies strategies and scores utility vs baseline. Metrics: %requests meeting quality threshold, cost reduction, latency distribution.
2) A/B: enable frugal_fidelity=low on 5% of non-critical routes and measure user engagement / downstream metrics (CTR, task completion). Short window (2 weeks).
3) Canary: controlled rollout on dedicated capacity to test autoscaling interactions and failure modes.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Cost/unit reduction: 20–40% token-equivalent reduction for low mode on autocomplete workloads.
- Utility retention: maintain >=85% of baseline utility (proxy: semantic-similarity to baseline output or human eval) for low mode.
- Latency SLO compliance: configurable per route; default target p95 < 250ms for low mode.
- Fallback rate: % requests that require escalation to higher-fidelity path < 10% (tunable).

API surface (rough):
- request param: frugal_fidelity: [auto, low, medium, high]
- optional: max_cost_tokens: int, latency_budget_ms: int, prefer_cached_prefix: bool
- response headers: X-RW-Frugal-Mode, X-RW-Strategy-Used, X-RW-Tokens-Estimate, X-RW-Fallback-Reason (when applicable)

Console UX ideas:
- Per-route toggle + projected cost savings (based on traffic profile)
- Heatmap for fallbacks over time with drilldown to example requests
- Quality regression alerts when utility delta exceeds threshold after a rollout

Open questions / decisions:
- What is the canonical confidence metric? (logit-gap? sidecar quality predictor? simple heuristics)
- Do we expose explicit strategy selection or keep it opaque? (transparency vs product simplicity)
- Billing model: do we bill strictly token-equivalent or have a "frugal surcharge"? Also how to price cached prefix benefits.
- Interaction with rollouts and canarying: should frugal modes be part of rollout policies or separate?

Next steps (short):
- Get buy-in from Applied ML (Sana) on quick confidence estimator feasibility
- Request anonymized traces from infra for simulated experiments (Evan)
- Draft minimal API change RFC and telemetry schema (this doc -> RFC)
- Mockup Console panel showing per-route projected savings

Notes to self:
- Keep this intentionally rough. Need to avoid duplicating "economy mode" branding used by other teams; frugal_fidelity focuses on composable heuristics, not single-knob quantization.
- Potentially a low-friction beta: expose as preview feature with default off and opt-in via API key label.

Fragments / todo bullets:
- quick-sim: run 24h trace for autocomplete route -> estimate savings
- build tiny confidence model (logit-gap baseline)
- design fallback catalog and priority list
- document privacy implications for Private deployments

Examples (brainstormed behaviors):
- User requests summary of a 3k token doc, mode=low -> runtime returns a concise 2–3 sentence extract using a micro summarizer; no full expansion.
- Chat assistant follows persona, mode=medium -> uses cached KV for last 2 messages and quantized small model for generation; if user asks follow-up requiring long-term memory, escalate to high.

End of sketch.
